title: Airgap KMS + Escrow POC — Data Safeguards Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working checklist and workshop notes for a customer-facing POC that must run in an air-gapped environment with customer-managed KMS and a third-party escrow requirement. Focus is on practical safeguards, minimal telemetry, retention limits, and DPA addendum bullets to accelerate legal reviews.

Context / constraints:
- Customer: regulated payments provider (apx SV), requires air-gapped runtime for PII flighting and model inference.
- Must support: Redwood Private (on-prem package) with customer network isolation, optional HSM/KMS integration (customer key material), and an escrow retention window for audit artifacts.
- No outbound traffic from inference nodes except to customer-approved aggregator.
- Minimal UX change for their devs: local SDK endpoint + offline ingest.

POC objectives (success criteria):
1) Demonstrate inference runs in fully air-gapped cluster with customer KMS wrapping.
2) Show that telemetry is strictly local and removable; no telemetry copy leaves the cluster.
3) Provide a DPA addendum draft that limits retention of artifacts to defined buckets and timelines.
4) Prove key escrow retrieval flow under controlled (audited) process.
5) Low-friction developer experience for model pinning and rollbacks.

High-level data flows (textual):
- Client app -> internal load balancer -> inference nodes (private VPC).
- Input tokens kept in RAM and KV cache; persistent artifacts only written to encrypted ephemeral-store (/var/redwood/ephemeral) with LUKS+customer-KMS.
- Audit logs go to local audit-collector service (only accessible to Security Ops). Audit collector writes signed, time-stamped artifacts into escrow-store (S3-replacement provided by customer) when explicitly requested by JIRA/legal.
- Model binaries pulled through customer-approved staging host (airgap transfer); hashes verified by integrity service.

Retention matrix (recommended defaults for POC):
- Input request payloads: 0 days persisted; session-local only. If customer requests retention for debugging, max 7 days with explicit ticket and TTL enforcement.
- Token-level caches (KV): in-memory only; persisted only for warm restart if customer opts in — max 24 hours and encrypted at rest.
- Inference outputs: considered customer data; retention 30 days by default for troubleshooting (opt-out).
- Audit artifacts (signed): retained in escrow for 90 days, only accessible with legal sign-off and key escrow release procedure.
- Telemetry/metrics: aggregated counters only, pushed to local metrics store; no PII-containing traces kept.

KMS & keyflow notes:
- Customer supplies root key material; Redwood components must use customer KMS/HSM APIs exclusively for envelope encryption.
- Private key never exported. Envelope keys can be rotated by customer; we support rotation hooks.
- Escrow key signing flow: audit artifacts encrypted with an escrow-wrapping key (customer-managed escrow HSM). Two-person release policy (customer security officer + Redwood compliance) for key unwrap in production.
- TODO: confirm support for PKCS#11 HSM on their appliance (ticket POC-212).

Escrow store design (operational):
- Escrow-store is an isolated object store managed by customer (S3-compatible).
- Only signed artifacts (SHA256 + attestation) written, with metadata index in local DB.
- Access flow: request->ticket->approval->temporary signed URL valid for 24 hours. All access logged.
- Escrow retention purge job must be automated and auditable; propose a weekly purge dry-run policy before hard-delete.

DPA addendum draft bullets (to hand to legal):
- Scope: defines types of PII and inference artifacts considered "customer data" during POC.
- Purpose limitation: retention only for debugging, security, or legal compliance; cannot be used for model training.
- Retention caps: input payloads 0d unless requested; debug artifacts 7/30/90 day tiers (explicit ticket required for longer retention).
- Key custody: customer retains exclusive control of master key; Redwood only uses envelope keys and does not hold master key.
- Escrow release: two-party release and timebound audit trail; Redwood agrees to notify customer within 24hrs of any attempt to access escrowed artifacts.
- Deletion verification: Redwood will provide delete receipts and hashes for erased artifacts upon request (X days SLA).
- Audit rights: customer can request on-site or remote audit of the POC infra and key handling processes with 14 days notice.
- Liability cap & breach notification: align with standard Redwood terms but add explicit notification timeline for escrow access.

Workshop runbook (90 minutes):
- 0–10m: Introductions, scope, desired demo points.
- 10–30m: Architecture walkthrough (airgap topology, KMS, escrow).
- 30–50m: Live demo (local SDK -> inference -> audit artifact generation) in staging airgap.
- 50–70m: Tabletop for escrow release & legal playthrough (who signs, timing).
- 70–85m: Technical deep-dive Q&A (HSM PKCS#11, TLS policies, network egress).
- 85–90m: Action items, ticket owners, next steps.

Open/risks/questions (work-in-progress):
- Q1: Are customers OK with 30d inference-output default? Some request 0d. Need product decision or per-customer flag.
- Q2: Is two-person escrow release acceptable to their legal? If not, propose time-locked escrow (e.g., 30-day delay) as alternative.
- Q3: Will the customer's legal accept our delete receipts as proof of deletion? Need to capture required format.
- R1: Network egress audit complexity — we must ensure no hidden egress (OS package checksums, DNS resolver leaks).
- R2: Performance hit for HSM envelope ops — need bench microdemo to show latency impact on 1–2s P95 budgets.
- TODO: assign bench ticket to infra (POC-212) and add telemetry whitelist for aggregated-only metrics.

Deliverables for POC:
- Implementation checklist (this doc) + scripted deploy for airgap runbook.
- DPA addendum one-pager + redlines for legal review.
- Mini-benchmark results for HSM-on-path vs HSM-off-path.
- Automated purge + delete receipt generator (proof-of-delete).

Notes to self / shorthand bits:
- "ephemeral-store" = LUKS partition + overlayfs.
- Keep SDK changes to config toggles only (no API surface changes).
- Keep an offline consent flow for debug retention requests (ticket-based).

Next steps (short-term):
- (Maya) finalize DPA bullets and circulate to legal by 2025-11-24.
- (Arjun) confirm HSM PKCS#11 compatibility with customer appliance by 2025-11-18.
- (Benji) add purge dry-run script and delete receipt prototype by 2025-11-26.
- (Sofia) schedule customer workshop 2025-11-30 and attach runbook.

Appendix: quick link map and references (working):
- POCs: POC-212 (airgap transfer), POC-240 (escrow flow), SEC-412 (KMS policies).
- Draft DPA addendum: quick bullets above — use as seed for legal redlines.
- Example delete receipt format (sample): artifact-id, sha256, deleted-by, deletion-timestamp, retention-ttl-was, approving-ticket

End of working checklist. This is intentionally iterative — expect edits after legal review and the first workshop.
